title: Compounding Growth
hook: Compounding is boring for months, then suddenly it's the only thing that matters.
statement: Build systems where the output feeds back in, so growth builds on itself.
explainer: A one-off sale starts from zero next time. A referral loop, evergreen content, or recurring revenue reinvests itself. It looks flat early, which is why people quit too soon.
sop: Sort your efforts into pay-once and pay-repeatedly.
Pick one compounding mechanism to build this quarter.
Commit to a fixed input and frequency for it.
Reinvest the output back into the same mechanism.
Review quarterly. It's invisible weekly and obvious yearly.
equation_example: PV is $1,000, growing at r = 10% for n = 5 periods. 1,000 × 1.10 to the 5th power = about $1,611. Higher r or more periods means way bigger results. A low r or stopping early mostly gets your input back.
question: Name one thing in your business you could set up to compound instead of starting over.
closing_statement: Small, reinvested inputs beat big one-time pushes.
caption:
Principle Nº 212: Compounding Growth

Compounding is boring for months, then suddenly it's the only thing that matters.

Build systems where the output feeds back in, so growth builds on itself.

Your turn: Name one thing in your business you could set up to compound instead of starting over.
